create.name: Arava Spiritual Center
create.bio:
The Arava Spiritual Center, known in Hebrew by the short name MOAR, is a Tibetan Buddhist and yoga community at Moa Oasis near Tzofar, in the desert of Israel's central Arava valley, a few kilometres from the Jordanian border. It was opened in November 2014 as a temporary home for the planned Ehvam International Spiritual Center for Peace, and its halls and residences were built by the students themselves with ecological methods. Its founder and spiritual director is Lama Dvora-hla (Dvora Tzvieli), who earlier set up a network of Dharma study groups across Israel, and the centre is run by a non-profit association called Method and Wisdom.

A community of around ninety students, including a small group of ordained monastics, gathers at the oasis for study terms through the year, learning Buddhist texts, meditation and yoga, and taking care of the site and its vegetarian kitchen together. Outside the terms many of them lead study groups elsewhere. Guests can join open evenings at the start and end of Shabbat, with singing, shared meals and talks by visiting teachers from different traditions, along with morning movement practice. Recordings of guided meditations and talks are shared on its YouTube channel, mostly in Hebrew.

free_resources.title: Shabbat with the Lama (open evenings)
free_resources.description: Open gatherings at the start and close of Shabbat in the centre's main hall, with communal singing, music, a shared supper and talks by students and visiting teachers from several traditions. A short body practice session, including yoga, is held on Saturday mornings. Advance registration is required.

Brief: hold for the owner. The same concerns bear on the existing lama-dvora listing.
